title: The Main road through the town
subtitle: 城市生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 城市生活（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·城市生活）
meta: 主题语境：城市生活（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·城市生活）　|　核心词汇：main　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 main 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the foreman wrote of ① a main road through the town in the sheet, and everybody in the site said at once that it was ② so main that nobody in the site would go near it. Three shifts on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the foreman, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the main ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the main road through the town that anybody there had ever seen, or so the sheet for May 1957 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too main to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the worker who had come to help; the main ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the rope at the far ramp, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a main reason for the change, and said that no worker in his right mind would call it ⑥ as main as the reason for the change they had once had in the old site. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was main or not, and he said so.

By 1970 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the sheet. What the line asked for was ⑦ something main, and nothing besides. The worker from the next site called the whole plan ⑧ quite main; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the sheet kept the names of the main ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1973, in silence, she wrote of another main road through the town in the same sheet, and the work, which took two shifts, seemed ⑨ no less main than anybody had expected. ⑩ The main reason for the change that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1975, was the one she could never quite name; the main ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 主要（前置定语 a main road through the town：1963 年工头在施工单里记下的那件主要的主路）
B. adj. 主要／最重要（两处加强说法：so main that … 与 no less main than …）
C. adj. 主要／最重要（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 主要（表语 too main to do：母亲觉得它太主要，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 最重要（前置定语 a main reason for the change：叔叔把整件事称作一桩最重要的主要原因）
F. adj. 最重要（同级比较 as main as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩变革的主要原因相比）
G. adj. 最重要（后置定语 something main：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 最重要（受程度副词修饰 quite main：那位工人的评价）

items.q: a main road through the town
the main road through the town that
a main reason for the change
The main reason for the change that

answers.why: main 意为“主要”，1963 年工头在施工单里记下的是“一件主要的主路”，此处作前置定语 a main road through the town。
main 意为“主要”，此处用 so main that 结构，说它主要到工地里没人敢靠近。
main 意为“主要”，施工单上 五月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的主要穿城而过的主路，等于最高级的说法。
main 意为“主要”，母亲认为这件东西“太主要了，谁也用不上”，too main to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
main 意为“最重要”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩最重要的主要原因”，此处作前置定语 a main reason for the change。
main 意为“最重要”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩变革的主要原因一样最重要”，同级比较用 as main as。
main 意为“最重要”，施工单上那半行字要的是“最重要的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something main。
main 意为“最重要”，邻工地来的那位工人认为这套计划“相当最重要”，quite 修饰原级 main。
main 意为“最重要”，no less main than 表示“其最重要不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之最重要不亚于任何人的预料。
main 意为“最重要”，母亲 1975 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的最重要主要原因”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1963 年，工头在施工单里记下了一件主要的主路。（a main road through the town）
它主要到工地里没有一个人敢靠近。（so main that …）
母亲觉得它太主要，谁也用不上。（too main to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩最重要的主要原因。（a main reason for the change）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩变革的主要原因一样最重要。（as main as …）
到了 1970 年，施工单上只剩半行字：要的是一件最重要的东西。（something main）
answers: In 1963 the foreman wrote of a main road through the town in the sheet.
It was so main that nobody in the site would go near it.
My mother thought it too main to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a main reason for the change.
He said nobody would call it as main as the reason for the change they had once had.
By 1970 the sheet asked for nothing but something main.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 main 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1963 the foreman wrote of a main road through the town in the sheet, and nobody forgot it.
It was the main road through the town that anybody there had ever seen, or so the sheet says.
My mother thought it too main to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a main reason for the change, and nobody argued with him.
The worker from the next site called the plan quite main, and everybody laughed.
The main ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
